quests.question: Fix: 'Me and Jake went to the cinema together last Saturday.'
quests.sentence: Me and Jake went to the cinema together last Saturday.
quests.hint: Use 'I', not 'me', when the pronoun is the subject of the sentence.
quests.explanation: As part of the subject, use the subject pronoun 'I', not the object pronoun 'me'. Also, convention puts the other person first: 'Jake and I went.'

quests.question: Fix: 'Between you and I, I think the plan needs a lot more work.'
quests.sentence: Between you and I, I think the plan needs a lot more work.
quests.hint: After a preposition like 'between', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: Prepositions (between, for, with, to, etc.) must be followed by object pronouns: 'between you and me', not 'between you and I'.

quests.question: Fix: 'The award was presented to she and her colleague at the ceremony.'
quests.sentence: The award was presented to she and her colleague at the ceremony.
quests.hint: After the preposition 'to', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: After prepositions like 'to', use object pronouns: 'her', not 'she'. 'She' is a subject pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'Whom is calling at this hour? It's far too late for phone calls.'
quests.sentence: Whom is calling at this hour? It's far too late for phone calls.
quests.hint: Use 'who' when the pronoun is the subject of the sentence.
quests.explanation: The unknown person is the subject performing the action 'calling', so use the subject form 'Who', not the object form 'Whom'.

quests.question: Fix: 'The teacher gave extra time to my partner and I during the exam.'
quests.sentence: The teacher gave extra time to my partner and I during the exam.
quests.hint: Test by removing the other person: 'gave time to I' or 'to me'?
quests.explanation: After the preposition 'to', use 'me'. Test by removing 'my partner and': 'gave extra time to me' is correct; 'to I' is not.

quests.question: Fix: 'Us students always prefer shorter homework assignments, if possible.'
quests.sentence: Us students always prefer shorter homework assignments, if possible.
quests.hint: When the pronoun is part of the subject, use the subject form.
quests.explanation: 'We students' is the subject of the sentence. Use the subject pronoun 'We', not the object pronoun 'Us'.

quests.question: Fix: 'She finished the course much more quickly than him.'
quests.sentence: She finished the course much more quickly than him.
quests.hint: In formal comparisons after 'than', use a subject pronoun.
quests.explanation: In formal English, use a subject pronoun after 'than': 'than he' (short for 'than he did'). 'Than him' is common informally but not standard.

quests.question: Fix: 'It was her who organised the entire farewell event for the team.'
quests.sentence: It was her who organised the entire farewell event for the team.
quests.hint: After 'it was', use a subject pronoun in formal English.
quests.explanation: In formal English, use the subject pronoun after 'to be': 'It was she who organised...' 'Her' is an object pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'The supervisor spoke to my colleague and I about the project deadline.'
quests.sentence: The supervisor spoke to my colleague and I about the project deadline.
quests.hint: After the verb 'spoke to', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'to' requires an object pronoun. Remove 'my colleague and': 'spoke to me' is right; 'spoke to I' is wrong.

quests.question: Fix: 'Him winning the competition made everyone in the department very proud.'
quests.sentence: Him winning the competition made everyone in the department very proud.
quests.hint: Before a gerund, use a possessive pronoun.
quests.explanation: When a pronoun comes before a gerund (a verb ending in '-ing' used as a noun), use the possessive form: 'His winning'. 'Him' is an object pronoun and cannot modify a gerund.

quests.question: Fix: 'Please send the report to either her or I by the end of the day.'
quests.sentence: Please send the report to either her or I by the end of the day.
quests.hint: After a preposition like 'to', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'to' requires an object pronoun: 'to either her or me'.

quests.question: Fix: 'The party invitation was addressed to both my sister and I.'
quests.sentence: The party invitation was addressed to both my sister and I.
quests.hint: Test without the other person: 'addressed to I' or 'addressed to me'?
quests.explanation: After the preposition 'to', use 'me'. A useful test: remove 'my sister and' - 'addressed to me' is natural; 'addressed to I' is not.

quests.question: Fix: 'To who should I address this complaint letter?'
quests.sentence: To who should I address this complaint letter?
quests.hint: After a preposition like 'to', use 'whom'.
quests.explanation: After prepositions, use the object form 'whom', not 'who'. 'To whom should I address this letter?' is the standard form.

quests.question: Fix: 'Her and Mark have been working on the joint project all week.'
quests.sentence: Her and Mark have been working on the joint project all week.
quests.hint: The subject of a sentence needs a subject pronoun.
quests.explanation: The subject of the sentence requires a subject pronoun: 'She', not 'Her'. 'Her' is an object pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'This is strictly between you and I, so please don't tell anyone.'
quests.sentence: This is strictly between you and I, so please don't tell anyone.
quests.hint: 'Between' is a preposition and always takes object pronouns.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'between' must be followed by object pronouns: 'between you and me'. 'Between you and I' is one of the most common grammar mistakes in English.

quests.question: Fix: 'Them arriving late caused major problems for the whole presentation.'
quests.sentence: Them arriving late caused major problems for the whole presentation.
quests.hint: The '-ing' form here acts as a noun. Which pronoun modifies a noun?
quests.explanation: Before a gerund like 'arriving', use the possessive form: 'Their arriving late'. 'Them' is an object pronoun and cannot precede a gerund.

quests.question: Fix: 'The coach selected my teammate and I for the regional competition.'
quests.sentence: The coach selected my teammate and I for the regional competition.
quests.hint: Test without the other person: 'selected I' or 'selected me'?
quests.explanation: Remove 'my teammate and' - 'selected me for the competition' is correct; 'selected I' is not. Use 'me' as the object.

quests.question: Fix: 'This is the shortlist of candidates who we would like to interview.'
quests.sentence: This is the shortlist of candidates who we would like to interview.
quests.hint: The pronoun is the object of the verb 'interview'.
quests.explanation: The candidates are being interviewed by 'we', making the pronoun the object: 'whom we would like to interview'. Use 'whom' when the pronoun is the object of a verb.

quests.question: Fix: 'It was him who left the window open throughout the cold night.'
quests.sentence: It was him who left the window open throughout the cold night.
quests.hint: After 'it was', use a subject pronoun in formal style.
quests.explanation: In formal English, use the subject pronoun after 'it was': 'It was he who left...' 'Him' is an object pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'The director wants to discuss the script with you and I next week.'
quests.sentence: The director wants to discuss the script with you and I next week.
quests.hint: The preposition 'with' demands an object pronoun after it.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'with' requires an object pronoun: 'with you and me'. Remove 'you and': 'with me' is right; 'with I' is wrong.

quests.question: Fix: 'The trophy was awarded to he and his co-author at the ceremony.'
quests.sentence: The trophy was awarded to he and his co-author at the ceremony.
quests.hint: Prepositions must be followed by object pronouns, not subject pronouns.
quests.explanation: After the preposition 'to', use the object pronoun 'him': 'to him and his co-author'. 'He' is a subject pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'Me talking on the phone during the meeting disturbed everyone present.'
quests.sentence: Me talking on the phone during the meeting disturbed everyone present.
quests.hint: When an '-ing' word functions as a noun, precede it with a possessive.
quests.explanation: Before a gerund like 'talking', use the possessive pronoun 'My': 'My talking on the phone'. 'Me' is an object pronoun and cannot modify a gerund.

quests.question: Fix: 'The decision to expand overseas directly affects you and I.'
quests.sentence: The decision to expand overseas directly affects you and I.
quests.hint: After the verb 'affects', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The verb 'affects' takes an object. Remove 'you and': 'affects me' is correct; 'affects I' is wrong.

quests.question: Fix: 'Ask either him or I if you have any questions about the process.'
quests.sentence: Ask either him or I if you have any questions about the process.
quests.hint: After 'ask', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The verb 'ask' takes an object pronoun. Remove 'either him or': 'Ask me' is correct; 'Ask I' is not.

quests.question: Fix: 'He shared first place in the competition with my sister and I.'
quests.sentence: He shared first place in the competition with my sister and I.
quests.hint: After 'with', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'with' requires an object pronoun: 'with my sister and me'. Test: 'with me' is right; 'with I' is wrong.

quests.question: Fix: 'We saw the exact person who the police were looking for that day.'
quests.sentence: We saw the exact person who the police were looking for that day.
quests.hint: Is the pronoun the subject or the object of 'looking for'?
quests.explanation: The police were looking for the person, making the pronoun the object: 'the person whom the police were looking for'.

quests.question: Fix: 'It's up to we parents to make sure the children feel supported.'
quests.sentence: It's up to we parents to make sure the children feel supported.
quests.hint: After 'up to', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The phrase 'up to' is a prepositional phrase and requires an object pronoun: 'up to us parents'. 'We' is a subject pronoun.

quests.question: Fix: 'My father is taller than him by about five centimetres.'
quests.sentence: My father is taller than him by about five centimetres.
quests.hint: In formal English, use a subject pronoun after 'than'.
quests.explanation: In formal English, the pronoun after 'than' in a comparison should be a subject pronoun: 'taller than he' (meaning 'taller than he is').

quests.question: Fix: 'I'm delighted that the opportunity came to my colleague and I.'
quests.sentence: I'm delighted that the opportunity came to my colleague and I.
quests.hint: After 'to', use an object pronoun.
quests.explanation: The preposition 'to' requires an object pronoun: 'to my colleague and me'. Test: 'came to me' is correct; 'came to I' is not.

quests.question: Fix: 'She performed much better than him in the final assessment.'
quests.sentence: She performed much better than him in the final assessment.
quests.hint: After 'than' in a formal comparison, which pronoun case is required?
quests.explanation: In formal English, use a subject pronoun after 'than': 'better than he' (short for 'better than he did'). 'Than him' is accepted informally but not in standard written English.
